topic.title: Basic Syntax & Data Types
topic.description: Master the fundamentals of C++ variables, types, and standard I/O.

questions.title: Variable Scope & Shadowing
questions.explanation: ::x accesses the global variable (10). The local x inside the block shadows the outer local x, so it prints 30.

questions.title: Integer Overflow
questions.explanation: Unsigned integer overflow is well-defined in C++. Adding 1 to the maximum unsigned int wraps around to 0.

questions.title: Prefix vs Postfix Increment
questions.explanation: a++ returns the original value (5) and then increments a to 6. So b=5. Then ++a increments a to 7 and returns 7. So c=7. a is now 7.

questions.title: Float Precision Truncation
questions.explanation: Assigning a floating-point literal to an integer truncates the decimal part without rounding.

questions.title: Char to Int Conversion
questions.explanation: 'A' has an ASCII value of 65. Adding 1 gives 66, which is the ASCII value for 'B'. Casting back to char prints 'B'.

questions.title: Const Initialization
questions.explanation: x is const so it cannot be modified. y takes a copy of x's value, and modifying y does not affect x.

questions.title: Auto Type Deduction
questions.explanation: x is deduced as int (usually 4 bytes). y is deduced as double (usually 8 bytes). Note: exact sizes can depend on architecture, but 4 and 8 are standard on 64-bit systems.

questions.title: Enum Values
questions.explanation: Enums start at 0 unless explicitly assigned. RED=0, GREEN=1. BLUE is set to 5. YELLOW automatically becomes 5 + 1 = 6.

questions.title: Namespace Resolution
questions.explanation: using namespace A brings A::x into scope. So x resolves to A::x (1). B::x explicitly accesses the variable in namespace B (2).

questions.title: Sizeof String Literal
questions.explanation: The string literal 'Hi' contains 2 characters plus a null terminator '\0', making its size 3 bytes.

questions.title: Boolean Output
questions.explanation: By default, booleans print as 1 (true) and 0 (false) in C++ unless std::boolalpha is used.

questions.title: Type Alias
questions.explanation: 'using' creates an alias for a type. Integer is identical to int.

questions.title: Hex and Octal Literals
questions.explanation: 0x10 is 16 in hexadecimal. 010 is 8 in octal.

questions.title: Static Cast
questions.explanation: static_cast<int> explicitly converts the double to an integer, truncating the decimal part.

questions.title: Extern Variable
questions.explanation: extern declares that the variable exists. It is then defined and initialized to 42.

questions.title: Modulus Operator
questions.explanation: In C++, the sign of the result of the modulus operator matches the sign of the dividend (the left operand).

questions.title: Character Arithmetic
questions.explanation: The ASCII value of '3' is 51 and '4' is 52. When adding them, they are promoted to integers: 51 + 52 = 103.

questions.title: Multiple Assignment
questions.explanation: Assignment operators evaluate right-to-left. 10 is assigned to c, then the result of that assignment (10) is assigned to b, and then to a.

questions.title: Macro Constants
questions.explanation: Macros are evaluated during preprocessing. x is assigned 100. Then MAX is undefined and redefined to 200 before being printed.

questions.title: Void Pointer
questions.explanation: A void pointer can hold any address but cannot be dereferenced directly. It must first be cast back to the correct pointer type (int*).
